newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil still in line with ACPC coffee export limit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil still in line with ACPC coffee export limit.

text.p: Brazil is on course to meet its six million 60-kg bag January-to-June coffee export limit agreed together with other producing nations, said a top government official after a meeting with exporters.
"We should be around six million bags, perhaps a little more, perhaps a little less," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.

There had been some concern a high level of shipments in the first quarter of this year together with export registrations for the April to June period would push Brazil considerably over the six million bag level.
However many of these registrations were now expected to be rolled over, said Oswaldo Aranha, head of Brazil's Coffee Exporters Federation (Febec).
"The feeling we are getting is that the volume of loadings and sales is dropping as we expected," Assis said.
Brazil in the first three months of this year sold 3.89 million bags according to Febec statistics.
Registrations for April were 1.64 million bags as of April 11 but only around one million bags is now expected to be actually shipped this month, Assis said.
Certainly loadings would appear to fit in with this forecast.
As of April 22, only 437,449 bags had been loaded against 801,070 by the same period last month. Certificates of origin for April to the same date covered 1.03 million bags.
One million bags in April would leave just over a further one million bags to be shipped in May and June and both Assis and Aranha felt that this was feasible.

The meeting with exporters did not reach any conclusions as to what should be Brazil's position ahead of a May 21 council of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) which is to discuss whether market stabilisation mechanisms should continue beyond June 1997.
The issue would be discussed at the next meeting of Brazil's new coffee council, the CDPC, on May 7 but there would be no definitive position ahead of the London talks, Assis said.
"The tendency for the time being is to continue (with mechanisms) but we have to see how the market behaves in the coming weeks," Assis said.
"But we will not have a definitive position before we get to London, we have to negotiate with our partners," he said.
